title: Suggestion/request: is it possible to make a solely client-side version of this?
body:
Hi, I've been looking through the code and understanding the client-server interaction, as I want to branch this and add a new capability.

Is it possible for this to run entirely client-side? I added some server logging and all I see is stuff related to the wikipedia requests. Does this NEED to run from the server, or could it be adapted to run clientside? I think having a PWA that didn't require any server would make this much easier to improve and distribute.

I'm sure this would be a fair amount of work, I just want to know whether it's theoretically possible, or if there is some constraint that means something needs to come from the server end.
author: davidwhewell

comments.body:
This app is essentially a front-end to the Wikipedia API - all of the app's content comes from there. The only way to disconnect it from the API is to clone some portion of Wikipedia's content into your app. Of course that would be a very small fraction of Wikipedia's total data, since the size of their English database alone is said to be around 156 GB. You could only fit a tiny portion of that into the limited storage capabilities of a PWA.

So... you could probably cobble something together that would sort of do this, but it wouldn't be very helpful and the data would get stale quickly.

Thanks for the reply, I don't think I made myself clear though - I completely agree the app would need to be "online" to get fresh content from wikipedia via its API. My understanding though is that this code as it is requires its own backend, running on the node/bun server. I put some logging into the server, and as I scroll the app I see requests going back to that, **so am I right, or have I misunderstood it?**

I think it would be great if the app didn't require its own back-end, and communicated directly with the wikipedia API from the app running in the browser. If that's not the case already!

(I haven't done front-end stuff since we had to care about MSIE in javascript, so sorry for the newbie question!)

I haven't looked at the code that closely, but if I understand your question it seems like it already does this. All of the app's run-time calls are made directly to the Wikipedia API. Did you perhaps clone the repo and start the dev version? If you want a clean standalone version, I assume you can just run `bun run build` as specified in the package.json. That should package up the standalone version you are looking for. But again, I haven't played with the code at all.

Also going back to your original comment:

> I think having a PWA that didn't require any server would make this much easier to improve and distribute.

This already has PWA support. It worked quite nicely on my Android phone.

I think this is better for the discussion tab and not the issues tab.
Do ```bun install``` followed by ```bun run dev``` and it should just work.
Also, this code has no backend! 
I made a folder called frontend and backend, but I deleted the backend when I realized I could make all the api calls via the frontend!
